nodes.title: AirLLM
nodes.summary: Runs large models on small GPUs by loading one layer at a time. A 70B model on 4GB VRAM at full precision, but slower.
nodes.notes:
- https://github.com/lyogavin/airllm
- Normally a 70B model needs around 140GB of VRAM. AirLLM loads one layer at a time into GPU memory, runs the computation, saves the result, then swaps in the next. A 70B model runs on 4GB VRAM at full precision.
- Like reading a book one page at a time instead of memorizing the whole thing.
- Speed is traded for accessibility. Slower than full-VRAM inference, but private and local on hardware you already own.
- Install with `pip install airllm`.

nodes.title: StrataLLM
nodes.summary: Runs 125B+ MoE models on consumer GPUs with dynamic sparse router offloading. Claims from the project page, not verified.
nodes.notes:
- https://stratallm.org/
- Claims a 125B+ MoE model (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 125B) on a single 12GB NVIDIA GPU and 64GB system RAM.
- Predictive sparse routing: predicts which expert layers will be called 1-2 tokens ahead and queues them for PCIe transfer.
- Tiered VRAM-RAM cache: critical attention heads and frequently used experts stay in VRAM. Dormant weights stream from DDR5.
- Zero-copy pinned memory: weights go over async CUDA streams into tensor cores, bypassing CPU compute.
